The entire staff, from reception, technicians, assistants, vets, and specialty vets, are simply the best. Their kindness and empathy is only trumped by their talent! 100% recommend!

Disappointing experience i had here tonight in the emergency unit. My dog was bleeding from the side of his face and all i got was towels,rudeness from the front desk lady and told that i had to wait. So i waited and waited mind you I came in at 7p and its already 1a wow. I ask again how long more still a wait. I left 6 hrs of waiting is way too long and my dog was bleding so that was not a priority!!!?? So please tell me you treat dogs like family. People do not waste your money here.
We received excellent care with our boy Buster!
Compassionate. Just expensive.

This is the second time I have had a major, difficult, and scary situation with one of my pets. One of my male cats got a blockage after having a UTI, and I had to bring him to MedVet four separate times over the course of a few days. As you can imagine, I was an absolute mess and so afraid I was going to lose him. MedVet really worked with me on costs and a home care plan for him, and I am so grateful for their entire team for giving him the best care that I could afford. Every person I spoke with came to the situation with professionalism and compassion, and answered all of my millions of questions and concerns clearly and honestly. I am hoping nothing else comes up for him, but know that if it does that I can trust MedVet to give him the best care and me the best options. These situations are never easy for pet owners, so having MedVet to help to navigate them truly makes all of the difference.
Everyone was so nice and showed great concern for my pet. They were professional and informative.

This place is all about money. They don't care about your dog. They make you pay all this money upfront knowing my dog had no chance to begin with. It's all a money grab. They didn't even cleanse/flush out or close all the small laceration and puncture wounds so they wouldn't get infected, they let bacteria settle in. My sweet dog was stapled together like a rag doll. They helped kill my dog, they gave me false hope, $12000 down the drain, just to call me back less than an hour later to basically tell me to come say my last goodbyes. I will never ever for get this. I was just about to send the staff a gift basket for my appreciation. However I am grateful to the staff who were nice and compassionate. I'm beyond devastated!!! Stop getting in these care professions and you all don't really care some of you all are a bunch of freaking tin men!!! There's an old Biblical saying treat people how you want to be treated, some of you all should practice it!!!

We brought our 18-year-old dog, Milo, in on a Sunday night after he suddenly collapsed and his breathing became very abnormal. From the moment we walked in, we were taken care of quickly and with so much compassion.

Dr\. Allison Kavanagh took care of Milo and was incredibly kind, thorough, and understanding. She explained everything to us in great detail and made sure we understood what was happening and what our options were.During such a frightening and emotional time, we were incredibly grateful that Milo was seen so quickly and that he was in such caring hands.

After having Milo as part of our family for 18 years, this was an especially difficult experience for us. We are so thankful to Dr.Kavanagh and the entire team for the care, compassion, and kindness they showed Milo and our family.We will always be grateful for the way they cared for him during such an important and difficult moment.
Caring staff, thorough triaging when in need of  ER care, knowledgeable specialists (oncology and neurology with two different dogs)
Very patient and helpful. I was freaking out and they took great care of my baby. She is doing much better.

After trying two different veterinarians for my dogs epilepsy, I discovered MedVet. We see Dr. Niman and he has the seizures under control now. It’s been two years since his last seizure. And prior to that, he was having them every 10-14 days. Life changing! I highly recommend.
Thank you for taking the time to leave us this amazing rating! Have a wonderful week!

This place is absolutely dreadful.  I waited 7 hours (basically overnight) for my cat to be seen when the estimated wait time was 3 hours.  They kept her in the back the whole time, and when we finally were called in to see the Dr. Alisha Fulton, she was dismissive, condescending, and rude. She only spent 5 mins with us after a 7 hour wait.

I have NEVER seen my cat so anxious and scared at any vet in my 11 years of having her.  We left with my poor senior cat in a worse condition than when we came and had to go to another emergency vet directly upon leaving.  We were still expected to pay hundreds of dollars for the appointment at Med Vet.

At a minimum if you choose to go to Med Vet, make sure that Dr. Fulton is not the MD you see.  You will not get good care.

I cannot recommend Dr. Luethy at MedVet highly enough. He has been the cardiologist for my last two pets, and I truly believe his care and guidance helped extend both of their lives.
What I appreciate most is his thoughtful approach. He explains what is happening, what we may expect, the likelihood of potential issues, and how best to manage them. He is equally thoughtful about when to treat and when not to. With my Pekingese, Mona Lisa, other veterinarians had recommended starting medications earlier, but Dr. Luethy knew when it was actually necessary—helping us avoid unnecessary expense and, more importantly, potential side effects.
He also looks beyond cardiology. When I had other concerns about Mona Lisa’s health, he recommended practitioners who could provide the right guidance rather than simply leaving me to figure it out.
Dr. Luethy has a wonderful manner with my pets, and his entire staff is incredibly gentle and loving with Mona Lisa. When my boy Luke passed away, the sympathy card from Dr. Luethy snd his team meant a great deal to me.
He combines expertise with judgment, compassion, clear communication, and genuine care for both his patients and the people who love them. I’m incredibly grateful to have him caring for my pets.
He combines expertise with compassion and clear communication. I’m incredibly grateful. and recommend him without hesitation.

From the first time I contacted Med Vet and scheduled the initial consultation appointment...our experience was great. The staff was friendly, knowledgabe, and professional.  The surgeon we consulted with was patient,kind and a thorough. The doc consoled me as I was freaking out a little,.She explained everything from pre- post op. instructions. Even had to explain some things twice as i was a bit infocused ,& pretty overwhelmed.  Staff Explained the risks and the tough recovery time as Rocks our pup will be undergoing double ACL surgery. Reasonably priced for double ACL surgery!!! 5 stars great choice...you won't be disappointed!
Michele/ aka Rocks mom

Wow, not only does Med Vet shift you from specialist to specialist, all at additional costs, but they don’t disclose that imaging only last so long. Our dog needed life saving surgery, but because his imaging didn’t meet their standards (which they actually lied, we caught them in the lie because it was… we know how to add and use a calendar) they need a new MRI @ $3,000.

Not animal advocates, just looking for money from desperate owners! Disclose your costs, disclose decision timelines, learn how to read a calendar, and do better!

We have always had amazing care from MedVet. Our cat Wendy has had numerous health issues over the year, and has visited numerous departments (oncology, optometry, surgical, and neurology). Every vet and staff member we have worked with has been kind, caring, and compassionate. We just know Wendy wouldn’t be doing so well today without MedVet. So thank you MedVet!!!

Dr. McAllister and staff are amazing. Their follow up and recommendations have made my six year old epileptic dog's seizures so much more manageable. We are able to call in with questions and call backs and emails are responded to so quickly helping ease our anxieties that we are caring for her the best that we can.
Great service!

The checkout process during my last visit to MedVet was not so great. After I was walked to the front to check out, I was taken back to the exam room and left waiting so long that I had to cancel my Uber and pay a cancellation fee. I then had to wait even longer for another ride.

I learned that the delay was because MedVet had decided to fill a prescription for my pet without asking me first. It would have been quicker to let me check out and send the prescription to the pharmacy on file, where I could have filled it for less.

When I raised the cost, the vet tech asked the checkout person how much the prescription was. The exchange made me feel as though I was being shamed for wanting to save money. The price at MedVet doesn’t change the fact that the pharmacy would have been cheaper, and the decision cost me time and an Uber cancellation fee.

I’ve been coming here for almost 6 years and the experience is usually great, but today was the exception.

My dog had a severe abscess that was leaking through her skin.  Surgery was done same day.  Vet and assistants were very thorough with their explanation of what was going to be done.  My dog stayed over nite and when I picked her up the next morning the Vet explained once again very thoroughly how and when to administer medications for upcoming days.  Nobody wants to deal with an emergency with a pet but I couldn’t ask for better care with mine
Vet technician Camilla and vet doctor Byrum were terrific with our border collie, Isla. Both were responsive, intelligent, thoughtful, and helpfully concerned.
Wow, thank you for the high star-rating!

Back in January 2026, my 14 year old cat who I've had since he was a kitten was diagnosed with an intestinal adenocarcinoma. Our primary vet at the time explained how it's aggressive and that we may want to consider palliative care and eventually euthanasia since it will likely result in a bowel obstruction in just a few weeks. However, she referred us to MedVet so we could get a more detailed scan and a specialist's opinion. We first saw Dr Mia Livaccari who was so nice and compassionate. After his scan at MedVet confirmed the diagnosis, she explained everything thoroughly, including the risks, and gave us the confidence to move forward with surgery and chemo.

The surgery was done by Dr. Elizabeth Krier and it went about as well as we could have hoped! He went on to get chemo every 3 weeks for, I think, 3 months. In that time, a new oncologist (Dr. Roberta Portela) took over his care who, like all the other doctors there, was excellent and took the time to answer any of our questions throughout his treatment.

After 3 months, his scans showed no recurrence of cancer. I think back to when he was initially diagnosed at his primary vet and how terrified I was that I might only have a few weeks left with him. The fact that we're almost at a year since his initial diagnosis and he's doing so well is a testament to the team at MedVet! I can't thank them enough!

After coming here several times with 2 different cats, I can say that MedVet is excellent for urgent / emergency situations, but not so much for less urgent, sick pet situations. If you can wait a day to see your regular vet, you should. MedVet is great because they do the labs / bloodwork while you wait. If your pet is in a life or death situation, definitely bring them here. Otherwise, go to your regular vet.
Gatta lotta respect for the team over here

The vets communicate very thoroughly about your pets condition and present options, since pet care bills can rack up very quickly. What an awesome staff everyone was so kind and supportive I would like to thank Dr.Salerno and his nurses I left there feeling so much better with buddy!!! And thank you for being kind hearted and showing so much kindness!! I will always be thankful and most definitely let everyone know that is a wonderful place to take your fur babies thank you again Dr.Salerno
Thank you for reaching out to us with such a great rating of MedVet Chicago! We strive to provide an excellent experience, and your opinion plays an integral part in making this happen! All the best!

The most caring, dedicated, veterinarians and support staff I have ever met. They care, and it runs from cardiology to rehab, somehow, they are always willing to go the extra mile. What a fantastic group across-the-board.

Unfortunately, my cat developed an eye problem, and we carefully selected a client because we needed a clinic that focused on eye diseases and wanted a doctor with experience. Dr. Smith works at this clinic, and he explained in detail the surgery and recovery process. Having surgery was a serious and difficult decision, but we took the plunge and are now in the recovery process. Thank you, Dr. Smith!
My dog has a heart condition and we started seeing Dr Reuter. She was great. She spent time explaining things in detail and they were all so caring for my dog.
Exceptional care was given to us and our dog Alex. Everyone was very nice, caring and professional.  All of our questions were answered in detail .Couldn't have asked for a better experience.
Thanks for your review! We strive to provide a great experience, and definitely appreciate your rating. Please don't hesitate to reach out if you need anything. Best regards!

Unfortunately our Corgi suffers from IVDD ( neck/spine nerve pain), and after several trips to Med Vet, we’re doing our best to keep “Fred” quiet and have minimal activity for 4-6 weeks.  Typically not easy for a Corgi, but with Fred’s pain, he’s not himself.  The staff at Med Vet have always been patient, knowledgeable and professional.  They listen attentively and never make you feel rushed.  They understand the fact that you’re at an emergency vet, is traumatic for you as a parent as it is for the pet patient.

My poor pup passed away yesterday. We rushed her to MedVet not knowing that she was in critical condition. They performed CPR on her but my husband got the sneaky suspicion that they knew she was already far gone when they performed "life saving measures." That's not why I dinged them. After my pup passed they moved my husband and daughter from and exam room and into what my daughter called a "dead puppy room." It was cold, didn't have a sink, had a metal table in the middle and had a price list and choice of cremation/keepsake options. My daughter described it best, if your human loved one passes in the hospital they don't automatically shuffle you to a room with caskets and urn options. It's a shame because that will be the memory that my daughter has of her first pup passing.

I brought my 16 yr old cat in who was in late stage CKD and having difficulty breathing very late Saturday night and after over 2 hrs of not even getting triaged and no communication we decided she appeared stable enough for the night and left without getting care. The next morning we went right back to the ER as she had not improved. This time was different, we told them about her struggling to breathe and the team immediately rushed her to the back and took her from us. It was a relief after being ignored the night before to be treated with such urgency. After awhile they brought us back and we spoke with the vet who was very patient and understanding of the plethora of previous diagnosis and concerns. We ran blood work and found out she was in kidney failure and the entire staff was so kind and sympathetic and gave us great resources. She passed a day later in our arms. I’m glad we took her here and how things worked out. I realize at night staffing is short and priority is skewed but I just wanted to share our experience. Always grateful for a 24hr emergency clinic but not receiving care or communication the night before was beyond frustrating. The morning team was amazing and we will definitely use this place in the future if needed. For now RIP Pepper 🐈‍⬛❤️

We took our cat here when she swallowed thread that was attached to a sewing needle and, while the staff was nice and the facilities clean, there were several issues:
1. We arrived and checked in within 30 minutes of the needle swallowing. We were seen by a vet tech for vitals relatively quickly and they told us they would take her back for an X-ray. We were told that she may be bumped in line for more emergent cases, but that they would bring her out to us if that were the case. After about 3 hours and checking in twice, a tech brought her out to us in the waiting area and said that they were still waiting on X-ray availability and had forgotten to let us know.
2. The hospital triages based on symptoms and emergency levels: immediate intervention(red), urgent intervention (yellow), and stable (green). Our cat was designated urgent, meaning intervention and observation were necessary, but not immediate. Understandable, and an estimate of 4-6 hours was given. We sat with her in the waiting area for another 3 hours while other pets that had come in after us and were designated as stable saw a doctor before us.
3. When we were taken to an exam room and our cat taken for an X ray, it was another hour or so before the vet came in. To be expected, she had a needle in her stomach. At this point, the vet informed us that the best option for removal would be endoscopy (going in through the mouth with a scope and a tool) under sedation. Again, to be expected and what we were waiting to hear. However, we were also told that the hospital’s anesthesiologist or sedation expert was “on call” and could choose to decline to come in. Generally, I would want any medical professional to be rested and feel that they could perform a procedure, but they had not even called them yet to ask if that was a possibility. We were then told that another option was to move our cat to another emergency vet center that has sedation on hand 24/7.  Frankly, that would have been nice to know 6 hours earlier.
We ended up taking her to the other emergency vet center and they went in, retrieved the needle, and got us out within two hours. So, we waited 6-7 hours, paid nearly $800 for them to confirm what we already knew, and ended up being pawned off on to another center. The good news is that our cat is 100% fine and back to normal.
While I am not a vet, I have experience with human anatomy, and the primary concern with ingesting a sharp object is always perforation. We were very fortunate that the needle didn’t perforate her esophagus on the way down, and that it remained in her stomach and didn’t work its way through her gastrointestinal system while we were waiting on an X ray.
I appreciate that emergency medicine requires triage and that every customer there was worried for their pet. However, whether it was a busy day, lack of communication, or general disorganization, the situation with our cat could have easily gone south, requiring surgical intervention. Which is ironic considering that they couldn’t guarantee that they would be able to have a staff member sedate her.
MedVet is a partner of our primary care vet, so I expected more and was very disappointed. In any future emergency, we will not be bringing our cats here.
Thank you very much for rating us so highly! We value your feedback and take pride in providing the best possible experience! Thanks again!
Very friendly and supportive staff. Took great care of our little fur-baby
The vet tech and surgeon were amazing with my fearful dog. Such clear expertise! Great communication.

I was recently at MedVet for the last day of my dog’s life. On one of the worst days of my life, every nurse and doctor I interacted with was patient, kind, understanding, and knowledgeable.

They gave me the time and space I needed, walked me through the options, and explained, very thoroughly, what each would entail. They helped with next steps and took care of payment and small details so I could spend every last second with my girl. Even though it was an utterly gut-wrenching decision to make, I felt confident in doing so because of the team I worked with that evening.

Thank you, MedVet, for taking such great care of my girl Rory in the last few hours of her life. I am forever thankful.

Our cat has spent a lot of time here because she has severe anemia and is immunocompromised. Every single time we go she gets the best care! Everyone is so helpful and kind to us and our girl. They are very attentive, empathetic, and keep us updated throughout her stays. Special shout to Dr. Victoria Lopez-Aldazabal for being the best vet and helping Sally so much!

On July 7th I brought my baby Pebbles to this hospital in the night. Doctor's told me she was in a really bad condition. They performed blood work and her condition was bad. I paid 4k just to have her checked and performs all the necessary checks. She was supposed to stay over night and if she stayed over night it would of been between 5k to 10k amd if she needed surgery it would of been between 15k to 20k and the next option would of been to euthanize my baby. I did leave her there and I was crying because she wanted to come with me. So the next day at 830am I picked her up and took her to her Doctor at Oak Elm Animal Hospital in Des Plaines. Her doctor told me "she is not looking good but I feel she will make it and I will do whatever it takes to help your baby" This doctor has miracles in his hands. He stayed with the doctor for almost 10 days and the charge was 4k and I went 2 days ago for her check up and thank God and this doctor my baby is healthy and no longer has anemia. He never mentioned anything about euthanizing her. He gave me hope and I trust him with my babies. Now my Pebbles is running and playing with his brothers and sister. Thanks to his doctor. Everyone, if you're not given hope and euthanizing is MedVet option. Please don't give up on your baby, take her to Oak Elm Animal Hospital. Don't give up on your baby without getting a second opinion.

After 3 days, princess is finally turning a corner back to wellness.

Had a great experience with Dr Leuthy! He is such a knowledgeable, patient and kind practitioner, even with tough news.
MedVet Chicago took good care of my cat when she was sick and consistently kept me updated throughout her stay.
I was seen on time and the vet was very knowledgeable and nice. I would definitely recommend Medvet to my friends. I believe my cat is already doing better.

Compassionate and transparent. My sweet cat had some complications which required specialty care, and I took her to MedVet regularly for a little over a year, including 2 emergencies. The team was always extremely kind and understanding, and the pricing was transparent. When a surgery was required, they gave me estimates, talked me through the options, and made sure I understood what would/could happen. They also recommended possibly more affordable options (academic veterinary centers) which was fantastic to see.

Unfortunately my cat needed euthanasia due to a deteriorating condition, and she spent her final days at MedVet. I received daily updates from the doctors by phone and felt that they cared about her well-being as much as I did. When it became necessary to put her to sleep, I was able to choose any appointment time I wanted, even into the night and early morning. The doctor who performed the injections was simply phenomenal. There was absolutely zero rush, zero talk about payments during that time, and they let me leave the building by a secluded side exit. I later received two hand-written cards from the care teams. I had an incredible experience at MedVet.

Thank you to Dr. Lopez-Aldazabal, Dr. Cohen, Dr. Dozeman, Dr. Blumberg, Dr. Matos, Dr. Kappesser, Juanita, Odalys, the Veterinary Social Work Team, the Critical Care Team, and all of the overnight staff.

I had a great experience at Med Vet. They got my dog seen quickly, explained everything clearly, and were kind and reassuring throughout  the visit. They were able to treat her successfully and the final cost was very reasonable compared with what I expected. I really appreciated the care she received and would definitely recommend them.
Thanks for your positive review! The whole team here at MedVet Chicago strives to provide a positive experience. Wishing you a great day!
They gave my capkey excellent care.
We love stars! Thanks so much!

DO NOT BRING YOUR PET TO MEDVET. I would never recommend this place to anybody after how they treated me and my dog during the worst moment of my life. Cold, money hungry, rushed and absolutely NO compassion.

My dog was having trouble breathing and instead of properly explaining what was happening, I felt pressured over and over to euthanize her. Pneumonia was mentioned, cancer was mentioned, her lungs were “foggy,” yet I left there STILL not knowing exactly what caused my dog’s condition. I had to beg for X-rays to be shown to me and even then barely got an explanation. I asked about other options and testing and felt like everything kept coming back to putting her down.

The WORST part was being put on a damn time schedule to euthanize my dog of NINE YEARS. When I asked to keep her another night and said I was willing to pay, I was told around $2,500 without them even giving me the exact price I asked for, then basically told there was “no point” and to euthanize her. MONEY was constantly brought up while I’m sitting there watching my baby die.

I signed for euthanasia, but I will forever feel like I was backed into a corner and given no real choice. I was scared, confused and grieving while they were rushing the most permanent decision of my life. I even wanted to hold my dog and felt like I had to fight for basic compassion during her final moments.

After she died I STILL couldn’t get clear answers about her cause of death. I also got conflicting information regarding a necropsy after initially being told about it as an option. By then my opportunity to get the answers I desperately wanted was gone.

And after ALL OF THAT, thousands of dollars later, I left without my dog, without the answers I begged for and traumatized by how her last hours were handled.

I’m not mad simply because my dog died. I’m mad about HOW MedVet handled it. I trusted these people with my baby and I will question her final hours for the rest of my life.

Ask for EVERYTHING in writing, get your records and X-rays, ask what is CONFIRMED versus suspected and get a second opinion if you possibly can. even tho I was referred here , by other vets unfortunately. They care they are good. I would go back and recommend.

Just came here to say, that over 3 years ago I took my, then, 10 year old cat to this place because she was in distress. When I brought her in she was panting. Which means heart failure. But after 30 minutes and no scans... no real time to assess her the vet came back and told myself and my partner at the time that my cat was in late stage heart failure. She was adminent my little girl had months to live. I lost my mind on her. If she reads this I'm sure she'll remember me.... I cussed her out six ways to sunday.... I knew my cat wasn't dying... I know her better than I know myself, she is my world. I asked to speak to the vet tech treating her and ask his opinion.... he said she was doing much better in the little time she was in the chamber and he thought she should go home. So she did.... 3 years later my cat STILL doesn't have heart failure... that tech saved me money and time...
When I was there they had a therapist on staff who sat with me almost the entire time.... she was amazing and I hope she got the hell outta this place.
Oh and turns out... my cat needed to take a shit she was constipated.  I paid 1500 dollars to cuss someone out.

Dr Gonzalez in Neurology was EXCEPTIONAL!!! The bedside manners are exactly what you need. She was so patient, kind and thorough. She would call me back with questions and helped with validation.

Kenny was AMAZING too! So kind and so much patience.

The rehab team was wonderful and so caring.

We had seen a few drs. Timing didn’t work out how we had planned for, and we ended up with the team above. I could have asked for anything better.

Dr Gonzalez and team, thank you so much for everything and taking care of us. We will always remember you and are forever grateful for your compassion, passion, and kindness. Thank you 🙏🏼
I’ve been here several times and cannot compliment them enough. They are caring, compassionate, honest. I always know I’m in good hands when I bring my pets here.

We had such a positive experience with Dr. Smith and the team at MedVet.

Our senior dog, Luca, needed to see a veterinary ophthalmologist, and we quickly realized how limited the options are in Illinois. Other practices were quoting us about a month to get in. MedVet already had the soonest appointment we could find at about two weeks, but what really stood out was how proactive they were about trying to get Luca seen sooner. The team kept in touch with us as earlier appointments opened up and ultimately got him in within just two days. That meant so much to us when we were already worried and trying to get him care as quickly as possible.

Dr. Smith was incredibly knowledgeable, but what we appreciated just as much was the time he spent with us. He explained what was going on in a way we could actually understand, walked us through the treatment plan and next steps, and was patient with all of our questions. We never felt rushed or brushed off.

The support staff was just as wonderful. Everyone we interacted with was warm, kind, responsive, and genuinely caring toward Luca. We ended up needing to bring him back again pretty quickly after his first visit, and once again the team worked with us to get him seen as soon as possible.

We’re really grateful for the care Luca has received from Dr. Smith and everyone at MedVet. It was a stressful situation, and having a team that was so responsive, thoughtful, and thorough made a huge difference for us.
Everyone there is nice and they make sure your pet is comfortable.
Thank you for giving MedVet Chicago such a great rating! It really means a lot to us. Thanks again!
Caring thoughtful and empathetic care

I am requesting that MedVet formally review Bunny’s entire case and provide an appropriate refund for the care and procedures that failed to resolve her condition and, from what we have observed, left her worse.

When our 14-year-old dog, Bean, started having cluster seizures, we rushed him to MedVet at 3 a.m., knowing he likely wouldn’t be coming home. We had planned for a peaceful at-home euthanasia, so I was devastated that his final moments would be in a hospital.

We called while we were on our way, and they had a stretcher waiting for us at the door. They immediately took Bean to the back for evaluation and, after asking us a few questions, brought my partner and me to a private, comfortable room.

The veterinarian came in to let us know that Bean had another seizure and explained what he believed was happening. After we shared that we knew it was Bean’s time, he assured us that we were making the right decision.

Then a woman (I regret that I got the names of no one who helped us) came in, explained our options and helped us choose an urn. After we signed some paperwork, they brought Bean in and allowed us to sit with him alone for as long as we needed. We were given a button to press when we were ready, and the vet came back in to help Bean pass peacefully. We were then given as much time as we needed to sit with him afterward.

As heartbreaking as that night was, every single person we encountered cared for all of us with such gentleness and genuine compassion.

Thank you to everyone at MedVet who was there that night (7/27/2026). I couldn’t be more grateful for our experience.
i brought my cat here after the urgent care couldn’t see him. everyone was very warm and kind and i know my baby was very well taken care of.

We should have just had my vet do Ollie's xray and it would have been determined that there were no broken bones. We would have saved Ollie from all the sedation and saved some money. At 9:26 PM my little Chihuahua fell off the bed and lost consciousness. I immediately grabbed him and rushed to the car while my wife searched for the nearest emergency clinic. When we arrived, he barely opened his eyes and slightly moved his head. We ran into the emergency room and explained the situation immediately. Blood was coming from his nose and it was obvious we were in panic.

What shocked us most was the complete lack of urgency and compassion.

The front desk employee acted extremely relaxed and slowly went through basic intake questions while my dog was still in critical condition. I fully understand protocols and paperwork are necessary, but in an emergency situation there should still be basic empathy and some sense of urgency.

When I asked if someone could at least briefly assess the dog to determine how serious the situation was, I was told, very casually, that “the dog is breathing.”

That response was incredibly upsetting considering the dog had been unconscious just minutes earlier.

After about 5 minutes of intake questions, we were told the wait time could be anywhere from 1 to 3 hours. During the next 20 minutes, nobody checked on us or asked about the dog’s condition. The only interaction we received was someone asking to take a picture of the dog for the waiting queue monitor.

Thankfully, during that time my dog slowly started regaining consciousness. We ended up finding another clinic with excellent reviews that agreed to wait for us before closing(they should be closed in 10 minutes). They immediately examined him and treated the situation seriously and compassionately.

That experience showed us what real emergency animal care should look like.

Thankfully, after examination we were told it is most likely a concussion and he should recover with monitoring, medication, and pain relief.

I sincerely hope this clinic improves the way they communicate with frightened pet owners during emergency situations. Because in moments like this, professionalism alone is not enough.

I am writing this review because I do not want another family to go through what we experienced on March 31, 2026.

Our cat Gray came in for an ultrasound, chest x-rays, and bloodwork. At 2 PM we received a call saying he was ready — but the intern physician on that call could not answer basic questions about next steps, what to expect, or whether a follow-up was needed. I asked to speak with the attending veterinarian when we came to pick him up and was told that would be arranged. It was not. When we arrived at 4 PM we were handed off to a vet tech instead, who also could not answer our questions. We left with no discharge paperwork, no instructions, and critically — no mention that Gray had been sedated or what that might look like at home.

We didn't receive the discharge paperwork until 5:49 PM, nearly two hours after we had already left with him and were home.

When we got home, Gray could not use his legs. He was dragging himself across the floor, falling over, and at one point appeared to stop breathing entirely. We were terrified and completely blindsided. My partner spent close to 30 minutes on the phone being transferred between staff at MedVet with no clear answer, while I simultaneously called our regular vet in a panic. We ended up driving back to MedVet's ER not knowing if our cat was dying.

The ER team was compassionate and excellent — and they quickly told us that this reaction was a completely foreseeable result of combining Gray's gabapentin with the sedation and opioids given during his procedure. That is the part I cannot get past. It was foreseeable. It was knowable. And no one told us — not during pickup, not in any paperwork, and not when we called in a panic.

Gray is our family. This wasn't about an inconvenience or a bill — it was about sitting on our living room floor not knowing if our cat was going to make it, when a simple heads-up at discharge would have prevented all of it. People come to MedVet because they trust you with the animals they love most. That trust has to be earned at every step — not just in the exam room. I hope you take this seriously, because no family should have to feel what we felt that night.
